properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 31 at 10:40PM CDT until July 31 at 11:15PM CDT by NWS Paducah KY
properties.description:
At 1039 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 7 miles southwest of St. Mary to near Alliance to 6
miles north of Buckhorn, moving southeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated. This storm has a history of producing tree
and powerline damage in Farmington.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to mobile
homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

These severe storms will be near...
Perryville, Patton, and Alliance around 1045 PM CDT.
Daisy and Millersville around 1055 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by these severe thunderstorms include Old
Appleton, Glenallen, Silver Lake, Lithium, Longtown, Sedgewickville,
and Oak Ridge.

This includes Interstate 55 between Mile Markers 110 and 139.
properties.instruction:
Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 31 at 10:36PM CDT until July 31 at 11:15PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
SVRLSX

The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Reynolds County in southeastern Missouri...

* Until 1115 PM CDT.

* At 1036 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles southwest
of Reynolds, or 34 miles southwest of Ironton, moving east at 45
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Corridon, Reynolds, Ellington, Centerville, Garwood and Redford.

This includes the following State Parks...
Clearwater Lake Recreational Area.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 1100 PM CDT for a portion of
southeast Missouri.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:52PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden, Three Rivers...Major
flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 39.2 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 39.0
feet on 10/21/2013.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued July 31 at 11:37PM EDT until August 1 at 12:15AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
For the following areas...
Waters from Savannah GA to Altamaha Sound GA out 60 NM...

At 1137 PM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line from
just south of Grays Reef Buoy to over Tug Rio Caroni, moving east at
10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
Tug Rio Caroni, John Bird and D R H Buoy.
properties.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with these storms.

NWSheadline: SPECIAL MARINE WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 1215 AM EDT

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 10:34PM CDT until July 31 at 11:45PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
At 1034 PM CDT, the thunderstorms producing heavy rain had ended.
However, flash flooding is likely to continue as the water drains
into creeks and rivers.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sullivan, Cuba, Bourbon, Anthonies Mill, Leasburg, Richwoods, Old
Mines, St. Cloud and Oak Hill.

This includes the following State Parks...
Washington State Park and Onondaga Cave State Park.

This includes Interstate 44 in Missouri between exits 203 and 218.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 9:29PM CDT until August 1 at 5:00AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Missouri...

Meramec River near Steelville.

River forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast
precipitation for the next 24 hours.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast due to heavy rain.

* WHERE...Meramec River near Steelville.

* WHEN...From this evening to late tonight.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 10.2 feet.
- Forecast...No forecast is available for this location.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Rainfall heavier than forecast could cause river levels to rise even
higher than predicted. The National Weather Service will monitor this
developing situation and issue follow up statements as conditions
change.

This product, along with additional weather and stream information,
is available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx
